[0] everyday_reading (E): In everyday graph drawings and in English, "a link between i and j" or "i j on a line" reads as a two-way connection, one record per line; in the input format the pair is ordered (i links to j only) and StdIn ignores line breaks, so pairs may be split or packed across lines.
[1] misconception (M) -> LinksAreSymmetric: wrong rule: The pair i j in the input means pages i and j link to each other. Right rule: Each pair is an ordered link from page i (the page containing the link) to page j (the page it refers to); 1 2 and 2 1 are two different links.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> LinksAreSymmetric: Applies LT (read N once, then read i then j per pass) unevenly: e.g. treating the leading N as the first link endpoint, or on some passes reading only one integer so i and j drift out of step and later pairs are read as (j, next i). (here mixing in: "The pair i j in the input means pages i and j link to each other")

[0] names_the_element (N): A data format (the list-of-links representation of a web graph): one integer N, the number of pages 0..N-1, followed by ordered integer pairs i j, one per link.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Pages are numbered 0 to N-1; the input stream holds N followed by pairs of integers, the first naming the page containing the link and the second the page it refers to; whitespace between tokens is arbitrary.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Transition reads N first with StdIn.readInt(), creates counts[N][N] and outDegree[N], then while !StdIn.isEmpty() reads i, then j, then increments outDegree[i] and counts[i][j]; the loop stops when only whitespace remains.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Reading the input yields integer tallies: counts[i][j] = number of i->j pairs and outDegree[i] = number of pairs starting at i; duplicate pairs count again, so tiny.txt gives counts[1][2] = 2 and outDegree = {1, 5, 1, 1, 2}.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One pass consumes exactly two tokens (i, j) from standard input and adds 1 to outDegree[i] and to counts[i][j]; no other entry changes and the tokens cannot be read again.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The tallies constrain the matrix: row i of the matrix is computed only from counts[i][] and outDegree[i], so a mistake in reading pair order (i/j swapped) moves probability mass into the wrong row.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): The graph is consumed through StdIn as whitespace-separated tokens: readInt() for N, then a !StdIn.isEmpty() loop reading pairs; each value is consumed once, so the read order fixes which number is N, which is i and which is j.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Data-driven code: keep the web model in a file and let a filter (Transition) read it from standard input, so any model can be studied without changing code; counts[i][j] and outDegree[i] act as per-cell counters (gatherers).

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> LinksAreSymmetric: Reordering the pairs or the whitespace layout keeps every count (the tally is order-independent); reversing a pair (j i) or adding a duplicate pair changes the graph and hence the page ranks.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use this list-of-links format whenever a web (graph) model is read as data and then turned into a dense N-by-N matrix; it does not scale to millions of pages, where the matrix cannot be stored and graph data structures (Ch. 4) are needed.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Page numbers must be in 0..N-1 (array index range). Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: A pair containing a page number >= N or negative: counts[i][j] or outDegree[i] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Every token must be an integer (readInt parses an int). Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: A non-integer token such as a page name (www.com) or 1.5 in the input: StdIn.readInt() throws InputMismatchException.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Links come in complete pairs. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: An odd number of integers after N: isEmpty() is false before the last i, then readInt() for j finds no token and StdIn throws an exception (NoSuchElementException).
wrong: The pair i j in the input means pages i and j link to each other. | right: Each link is an ordered pair: i j means a link from page i to page j only.
The links read from input fill counts[i][j], and each row of the transition matrix is built from those counts.
The graph is read from standard input: first the number of pages n, then the link pairs i j.
The links read from input are counted in a two-dimensional array, counts[i][j].
